$schema_note: Stacking rules for the final layer set (v1.0.0). Read with layer-tokens.json. 'base:' refs point into the nearshore base tokens.

z_order.note: nearshore house base (depth ramp × shade, bottom tint, piles) — never hidden; desaturated while a colour field is on
place, contour, pile labels with the house halo

blend_modes.all: normal (source-over). Never multiply or screen: multiply muddies the depth ramp, screen washes out light land.

precedence.rule: One colour field. The most recently switched-on fill layer owns the colour-field slot. A layer that loses it keeps only its non-fill representation (currents → streamlines, wind → particles or barbs, waves → arrows); a layer with no other representation (SST, chlorophyll, Kd490, salinity, subsurface, visibility) is switched off and its row says which layer replaced it.

One particle layer. Currents streamlines own the particle slot whenever currents are on; wind particles draw only when currents are off. When currents are on, wind draws as barbs (layers.wind.barbs) in the arrow/barb slot.
One arrow/barb layer. Wind barbs take precedence over wave direction arrows; while wind barbs show, waves keep only their fill (if they own the fill slot).
One veil. Cloud veil and sea-ice veil never together (sea ice is not local; it never auto-enables). The cloud veil caps at veil_cap_with_field_or_radar while a colour field or radar is on.
At most two isoline sets; the second is dashed. With SST fill on, its auto isotherms (from isolines_from_zoom) count as one set.

While any isoline, particle or arrow/barb layer is on, SST band edges are hidden; while a colour field is on, unranked atlas dots are hidden and kelp drops to layers.kelp-habitat.kelp.opacity_with_color_field.

STACK-A.name: Offshore bite (SST + currents + wind)

layers.why: P1: SST owns the fill slot
P1 + P2: SST owns the fill, currents own the particle slot

STACK-A.legend: SST °F · white lines = current · barbs = wind kt

NEAR-D.name: Nearshore z13 full stack

layers.why: P6: kelp at opacity_with_color_field; shore lines off in this preset
P6: unranked dots hidden under a fill

NEAR-D.legend: z13: fill + isotherms + kelp + ranked spots

what_they_are.CUR-C: speed colour FILL (cmocean speed, 0–1.2 kt) + white STREAMLINES (particle-class flow lines)
what_they_are.WIND-A: Windy-style colour FILL over land + white PARTICLES

violations: colour-field cap 1 (SST-B + CUR-C fill + WIND-A fill)

stacking_check.resolution: No cap or opacity changed. Two precedence rules made explicit (P1, P2): SST keeps the fill; currents drop their speed fill and keep white streamlines (the particle slot); wind drops fill and particles and draws barbs (the arrow/barb slot). This is the least change: STACK-A's approved image already showed wind as barbs, so only the current lines change look (CUR-B ink streaks → CUR-C white streamlines).

NEAR-D_final.note: no currents or wind in NEAR-D, so CUR-C/WIND-A do not affect it

other_fixes: P3: the draft let wave arrows and wind barbs show together (2 arrow/barb layers); wind barbs now win.
P6/kelp: KELP-D's approved solid canopy (0.65, 0.55 under a fill as in the approved NEAR-D) is kept as a named exception to the old '≤0.35 habitat fill' rule, which now applies to zones and AIS only.
Cloud veil: CLOUD-A's approved 0.92 max alpha is kept to z10, fading to 0.45 at z13 (draft curve 0.9/0.7/0.45 contradicted the approved look).
